title: Free Night Awards Interpretation Note: Rolling Twelve-Month Elite Nights on Returned Later Nights
content:
**Rule.** For one of the Free Night Awards returned from a later night of a reservation cancelled after its deadline, the night reduction of the protected rebooking price is the upper return night reduction when the elite night credits posted to the member's Ashbury Rewards account in the last twelve months are at least the upper return night threshold, the lower return night reduction when they are at least the lower return night threshold, and nothing otherwise. It is taken off the protected rebooking price once.

| Elite night credits posted in the last twelve months | Night reduction |
|---|---|
| At least 60 nights (upper return night threshold) | 1500 points (upper return night reduction) |
| At least 30 nights but fewer than 60 (lower return night threshold) | 500 points (lower return night reduction) |
| Fewer than 30 nights | No night reduction |

**Counting points.**

1. The last twelve months are the credits posted fewer than twelve whole calendar months before the return, each credit counted from its posting date to the date of the return.
2. Stay credits and card anniversary credits count alike: every night credit posting in the window is added by its nights.
3. A year-end reset of the night count is not a credit and takes nothing away.
4. The membership's count of elite night credits for the current calendar year is not the measure.

**Example (hypothetical account, return dated in March).** In the twelve months before the return the account shows night credits of 18 and 22 nights for stays posted the previous October and November, a card anniversary night credit of 15 nights posted in January, and the year-end reset of 31 December. The credits add up to 55 nights: at least 30 and fewer than 60, so the night reduction is 500 points. The membership's calendar-year count, 15 nights, is not used, and the reset takes nothing away.
